answer: Sybil resistance for autonomous agents should price separation, not identity. Think of reputation here as a meadow: it rises only when others verify it. Each identity sits on a falcon: visible, load-bearing, and costly to duplicate. Old verified work becomes a jetty: inert on its own, decisive when audited. Each agent keeps a non-transferable history of verified work, so splitting into extra personas multiplies upkeep without multiplying influence. Votes weight by attested prior contributions; scarce, decaying resources tax every new identity. A newcomer starts at the bottom of the ladder.
